A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their main text, equations, three figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison. Some reference URLs are clipped in v3, but the cited works remain identifiable.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical constructions, complexity results, and proofs, including in its appendices, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical. Its additional decidability argument is a mathematical result, not an empirical outcome.

M1.justification: The encoder computations, attention mechanisms, neural-network gadgets, and tiling-checking constructions are retained. Renaming SAT/BSAT and clarifying the existing fixed-width class do not introduce a new computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation tasks. The retained octant-tiling problems serve as mathematical reductions, not experimental benchmarks.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Prior transformer and verification systems remain related-work citations.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Precision restrictions and unary/binary encodings specify theoretical problems rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, or empirical robustness analyses. The retained verification and spam-detection examples illustrate formal-reasoning problems.

E5.justification: Repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, and other empirical uncertainty estimates are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, rankings, or qualitative experimental findings. The added decidability result is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 5 changes from NEXPTIME-hardness alone to decidability plus NEXPTIME-hardness for the general fixed-width class. Section 5 and Appendix C add an argument using periodic positional representations under wrap-around and eventually constant representations under saturation, substantively extending the formal decidability guarantee. Section 2 also adds a threshold-formulation equivalence. Theorem 3's NP/NEXPTIME completeness results already existed in v2; their stronger overview wording is not a new result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: undecidability for expressive encoders, decidable bounded-input and quantized cases, and high complexity. Quantized decidability was already advertised in v2; the new argument strengthens its formal support.

C2.justification: v3 explains that fixed-width arithmetic also restricts positional information, forcing periodic or eventually constant embeddings. Appendix C explicitly cautions that an exponentially large period prevents inferring NEXPTIME membership from this argument. The existing hardmax-versus-softmax limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The explicit network constructions and bit allocations in Appendices B–C are retained. No implementation, hardware, training, or code/data-access information is introduced; the added material concerns mathematical justification.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. The added reminder distinguishing encoder-only models from encoder-decoder models reiterates an existing distinction; citation formatting changes do not add related work.

P1.justification: v3 renames SAT/BSAT to TRSAT/BTRSAT throughout, updates publication and affiliation text, expands selected explanations, and condenses the conclusion. It preserves the section and appendix organization and most prose.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, places the general fixed-width case in the decidable region, and states that its hardness is not visualized. Figures 1 and 3 retain their content but move from pages 3 and 6 to pages 4 and 7. Bibliography reformatting causes several URLs to extend beyond the page edge.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies missing formal support for general fixed-width decidability in Theorem 5 and Appendix C, clarifies the remaining upper-bound limitation, and aligns the overview with Theorem 3's existing completeness results. These improve completeness and consistency while most constructions and proofs remain unchanged. The gains outweigh minor presentation regressions, particularly clipped reference URLs.
